channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold trades below $4,000 as stronger US Dollar, hawkish Fed outlook weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles below $4,000 on Friday as rising Oil prices revive inflation concerns and reinforce expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could raise interest rates later this year.

item.title: European Central Bank: Holds fire as September stays live – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect the European Central Bank (ECB) to keep the deposit rate at 2.25% in July after June’s hike, with September remaining a live meeting.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains on surging Oil prices, USD/CAD eyes second weekly loss
item.description: USD/CAD trades under pressure on Friday as the Canadian Dollar (CAD) benefits from higher Oil prices, offsetting the US Dollar’s (USD) recovery. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.4022, near a one-month low.

item.title: UK: Andy Burnham outlines pro-business Labour, inflation plan
item.description: UK Labour leader Andy Burnham said on Friday that he intends to lead a pro-business Labour Party, arguing that his experience working with businesses as Mayor of Greater Manchester will serve as the model for his future government, according to Reuters.

item.title: British Pound: Overvaluation points to Euro recovery – ING
item.description: ING strategist Francesco Pesole notes that the recent GBP rally has stalled and EUR/GBP has rebounded from an important break lower. At 0.850, the cross remains around 1.5% undervalued versus ING’s short-term fair value model.

item.title: European gas: Prices stay elevated as supply tightens – Commerzbank
item.description: Norman Liebke at Commerzbank expects European gas prices to remain high in the near term, even if the Strait of Hormuz reopens sustainably.

item.title: US Dollar: Energy shock may delay renewed downtrend – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes that ongoing Middle East conflict, stronger United States (US) data and crude Oil risks are limiting US Dollar (USD) selling. Better manufacturing and retail figures have not shifted Fed expectations much, but a full hike remains priced by year-end.

item.title: UoM Consumer Sentiment Index set to improve further but remain at historically low levels in July
item.description: The University of Michigan (UoM) will release the preliminary estimate of July’s Consumer Sentiment Index on Friday.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Under pressure against Euro but story intact – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky reports a broad risk-off move in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE), with elevated Oil and higher core yields pushing CEE rates up. Hungarian assets have suffered heavy selling, which he links to crowded longs and profit-taking.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar weakens as US strikes on Iran fuel risk aversion
item.description: NZD/USD declines on Friday, trading around 0.5830 at the time of writing, down 0.19% on the day, as investors seek safe-haven assets following a fresh wave of US strikes against Iran.

item.title: European Central Bank: September hike risk assessed – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Anatoli Anenkov expects no policy change at next week’s European Central Bank (ECB) meeting, with the central bank reiterating its data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach. Recent Euro Area data, including Germany and France, have not significantly altered the outlook.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Sideways trading extends with 1.1480 holding bulls
item.description: The Euro (EUR) records mild losses against the US Dollar (USD) for the second consecutive day on Friday. The EUR/USD pair trades at 1,1430 after being capped at 1.1480 earlier this week, extending the sideways trend, as geopolitical tensions and higher oil prices keep Euro rallies subdued.

item.title: British Pound: Sterling rally against Euro looks stretched - TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Macro Research team, led by Howard Du with contributions from Jayati Bharadwaj and Linda Cheng, argues that the recent Pound strength versus the Euro has overshot fundamentals.

item.title: US Dollar: Steadies on risk-off flows – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes that the Dollar has recovered part of this week’s losses as a tech-led equity selloff spurs a modest flight to safety.

item.title: Indian Rupee gains temporary ground, higher oil prices keep upside limited
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades marginally higher against the US Dollar (USD) while entering the weekend. The USD/INR pair ticks down to near 96.30 as the Indian currency rises, following Reserve Bank of India’s intervention.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Intervention risk keeps Franc lagging – OCBC
item.description: OCBC Bank strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note the Swiss Franc (CHF) has lost much of its safe-haven appeal as Swiss National Bank (SNB) intervention risk and low yields weigh on performance.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: British Pound extends weakness in process of UK leadership change
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) extends its decline against the US Dollar (USD) for the second straight day on Friday, trading 0.4% lower to near 1.3427 during the European trading session on Friday.

item.title: Australian Dollar declines as Middle East tensions boost the US Dollar
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.6970 on Friday at the time of writing, down 0.36% on the day, as the Australian Dollar (AUD) comes under pressure for a second consecutive day amid renewed US Dollar (USD) strength. Despite the latest pullback, the pair is still on track for a third consecutive weekly gain.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD hovers below $4,000 with the YTD low at hand
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) shows moderate gains on Friday, but remains close to the year-to-date lows, at the $3,940 area, with upside attempts capped below the $4,000 psychological level for now.

item.title: Iran’s IRGC warns of increased aggression on Washington and countries having US bases
item.description: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warns of "more crushing" retaliation during the European trading session against the United States (US) and countries supporting it for hosting its bases.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $55.44 per troy ounce, down 0.17% from the $55.53 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: BoJ to leave interest rates in July policy meeting - Kyodo
item.description: According to a Kyodo News report, the Bank of Japan (BoJ) is expected to keep interest rates unchanged at 1% in the July policy meeting, people familiar with the matter told. The report also showed that the central bank will likely raise its growth forecast for the year.

item.title: Japanese Yen drifts lower against the US Dollar and draws closer to 40-year lows
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) ticks lower for the second consecutive day against the US Dollar (USD), reaching the 162.50 area on Friday, drawing closer to the 40-year low, at 162.84 hit earlier this month.

item.title: European Central Bank: Rates on hold but tightening bias – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Jan von Gerich expects the European Central Bank to leave policy rates unchanged at the July meeting, describing it as a pause rather than a shift in stance. Lower-than-expected June inflation and volatile Middle East developments reduce urgency for an immediate move.

item.title: British Pound: Bearish against Euro on hawkish ECB guidance – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists see asymmetric downside risks for the British Pound (GBP) against the Euro (EUR). They argue that EUR/GBP appears notably undervalued relative to rate differentials, data surprises and equity performance.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Homeward investment shift could support recovery – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny highlights that the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains near cyclical lows, but Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF) and Japan Trusts flows already show a shift back toward JGBs.

item.title: Silver price on track for weekly decline as Middle East tensions fuel rate-hike worries
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $55.50 at the time of writing on Friday, virtually unchanged on the day, but remains on track to post a weekly loss of nearly 7%.

item.title: US Dollar: Smile narrative supports gradual gains – OCBC
item.description: OCBC Bank strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that the US Dollar (USD) remains supported by its yield advantage and safe-haven status, with FX moves still fitting the USD smile framework.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Consolidates near $79.00 before the next leg up amid bullish setup
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – extends its sideways consolidative price moves for the fourth straight day and trades around the $79.00 mark through the first half of the European session on Friday.

item.title: Brazil: Tariff fallout shapes election dynamics – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Dan Pan assesses new United States (US) Section 301 tariffs on Brazilian exports, noting a 25% levy effective 22 July that could rise to 37.5%.
